clue.text: He wrote 'Ben is Reformed'

definitions.note: a writer is meant: the clue names a dramatist by what he did

indicators.note: something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A playwright is credited with a work titled 'Ben is Reformed'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' looks like part of a play title, but it rearranges BEN IS. The Norwegian dramatist wrote A Doll's House and Peer Gynt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian playwright of Hedda Gabler is a famous author, so 'He wrote' points to him.

clue.text: A coloured band

parts.note: read plainly, a long narrow strip of colour on a flag, shirt or animal's coat

explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow line of colour on cloth or fur is exactly such a band.

clue.text: Athenian fellow in no matter what element

indicators.note: the word in places the Athenian fellow inside the phrase that follows it

parts.note: any, as in 'any one at all, no matter what'
Timon of Athens, the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A man from Athens is caught up in some unspecified chemical matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athenian fellow' is Shakespeare's misanthrope, from the play Timon of Athens; 'in' puts him inside the word for 'no matter what'.
explanation.definitionFit: The metalloid with symbol Sb is a chemical element.

clue.text: A German city boy catches up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom upwards, so the run is turned round

parts.note: a lad is a boy
nets, as a verb, catches (fish, a ball)

explanation.surface: In some German town a lad grabs hold of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run LADNETS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stendal is a town in Saxony-Anhalt, from which the novelist Stendhal took his pen name.

clue.text: Helper in the theatre must be less tardy

definitions.meaning: the person in the wings who feeds actors forgotten lines
more punctual, the comparative of an adjective meaning on time

explanation.definitionFit: One backstage aide feeds lines to actors, and the same word is the comparative of 'punctual' in another sense.

clue.text: The simpleton is French so finds a supporter

parts.note: an ass is a fool or simpleton
taken as written
tant is French for 'so (much)'

explanation.surface: A fool is described as French and thereby gains a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper or aide gives support to someone, so is a supporter.

clue.text: Pig-headed beast-into conversion

indicators.note: a conversion turns one form into another, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stubborn creature undergoes a transformation into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn and unwilling to be persuaded is what both words mean.

clue.text: Flatten reporters!

explanation.definitionFit: To squash flat is to iron or squeeze, and journalists as a body are 'the' newspapers' people.

clue.text: Little brother, ten, displaying liveliness

parts.note: Br is the short form of brother
10 written as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A small boy of ten years shows plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals an abbreviation; ten is 1 and 0, read as letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour and spirit, a word borrowed from Italian, is a synonym of liveliness.

clue.text: With little backing no-one makes application

parts.note: petit is French for small

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the following letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone without much support finds nobody makes a request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' is French here; 'backing' turns round only the 'no' and 'one' pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written request to an authority is an application.

clue.text: Marine forced to stay behind

indicators.note: forced suggests being pushed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marine is ordered to stay back at base.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue in a place after others have gone is to stay behind.

clue.text: A noble guy in a rather obvious way

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone acts nobly, but rather too showily.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across ratHER Obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave and admirable man is a hero, the noble figure of legend.

clue.text: Getting a RAF officer to say he's a traitor

parts.note: PO is Pilot Officer, a junior RAF rank
to state is to say

explanation.surface: An RAF officer is made to declare himself a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons their faith or cause is a deserter or traitor to it.

clue.text: Devil-worshippers replacing 6

indicators.note: replacing means putting the letters back in a different place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 6 down, a word for an aide

explanation.surface: Followers of the devil take over from a supporting player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' rearranges the letters of the answer at 6.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who worship the devil are followers of Satan.

clue.text: On the road, yet case is badly organised

indicators.note: something badly organised is in a muddle, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Out on the road, though, the luggage is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly organised' rearranges YET CASE. The answer is the reflecting stud set into a road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflective studs set in the road surface are what the clue points to, so 'on the road' describes where they sit.

clue.text: Giving guidance, though always in pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
e'er, poetic for ever, always

explanation.surface: Offering advice even though one is constantly suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' gives a poetic contraction of ever, which 'in' puts inside the word for pain; 'though' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Directing the course of something or someone is giving guidance.

clue.text: Gold found in a river or stream

indicators.note: found in means the first piece is located within the second

parts.note: the Trent, a major river of the English Midlands
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold has been discovered in a river or brook.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold is the heraldic word, and 'a river' is the Trent, which flows through the English Midlands; 'found in' places the gold within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast, powerful flow of water is a rushing stream.

clue.text: One may look well as a result of his ministrations

definitions.text: One may look well as a result of his ministrations

parts.words: One may look well as a result of his ministrations
parts.note: 'look well' seems to mean appear healthy, but means see clearly, thanks to the eye professional who fits glasses

explanation.definitionFit: A person who tests eyes and supplies spectacles helps clients see well.

clue.text: Common man who has attained high rank

definitions.text: man who has attained high rank

explanation.definitionFit: Widespread or usual is one sense; a top army commander is the other.

clue.text: Inexperienced driver-one on a charge for causing damage

definitions.note: a phrase where the answer is a verb: to damage by tearing

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British novice driver's car
an ace is a one in cards
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A learner driver is charged with damaging property.
explanation.walkthrough: Learner drivers in Britain display a red L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear flesh roughly is to wound or do damage.

clue.text: The president died where most people do

definitions.note: 'do' stands for 'die' from the clue's wordplay part: in bed is where most people die

parts.note: Abe, Abraham Lincoln, US president
d is the abbreviation for died in dates and records

explanation.surface: Lincoln died in the same place most people end their days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' repeats the verb 'died': most people die in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: In bed is the place where most people die, the clue's wry point.

clue.text: Trim and tie-dye, disregarding the directions given

indicators.note: disregarding means leaving out, so letters are taken away

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction; two of them here

explanation.surface: Neat and tie-dyed, ignoring the instructions provided.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the two Es from TIE-DYE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and well kept is what trim means as an adjective.

clue.text: Mild as can be so depressing

indicators.note: can be suggests what the letters might become if rearranged

explanation.surface: Something as gentle as possible can still be gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and cheerless is a synonym for depressing.

clue.text: Reveals a certain measure is to be taken in back-street

indicators.note: taken in means the measure is held inside the other piece
back means the abbreviation for street is turned round

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: Someone discloses that a measurement is taken in a side alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' does two linked things: 'back' turns round the abbreviation for street, and 'taken in' puts the old cloth measure inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Discloses or makes known is a synonym for reveals.

clue.text: Only the Ash, the bonnie Ash/Burns — while it is green" (De La Mare, "Trees")

clue.text: Last to include many a woman, it's realised

indicators.note: to include means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: end, the last part
C is the Roman numeral 100, many
she, a woman

explanation.surface: A woman is finally included, and it dawns on her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'realised' is the money sense, as converting an asset to cash; 'to include' splits the word for last around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned into money, as a cheque is cashed in, is a sense of realised.

clue.text: A gem worth fourteen pounds

definitions.meaning: the British unit of weight equal to 14 pounds

explanation.definitionFit: A jewel is one sense; the British weight unit of fourteen pounds is the other.

clue.text: Offering friend a roll that's appetising

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a table is a list or roll

explanation.surface: A friend offers a bread roll that looks tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like bread but means a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant to taste is a synonym for appetising.
